
  Here in the left, a faithful editor glows,
  Where functions bloom in syntax-tinted light,
  While on the right, a stream of output flows,
  And unit tests are running through the night.

  Down at the bottom, htop paints the load,
  In bars of green and amber, row by row,
  While git awaits to stage the latest code,
  And server logs in quiet rhythm grow.

  Across the footer runs the status bar,
  A ribbon stitched with clock and branch and host,
  That tells us who we are and where we are,
  When wandering through the machines weghost.

  Then thunder strikes—the wireless link is torn,
  The coffee shop's unsteady router dies,
  The laptop sleeps until the coming morn,
  Yet on the distant box, the session flies.

  Unharmed by broken pipes or dropped ssh,
  The daemon guards the child processes well,
  Compiler jobs still churn their steady way,
  Inside that phantom, unattached shell.

  We wake, log in, and type attach -t main,
  And in a blink, the workspace is restored:
  Each split, each scrollback buffer, every pane,
  Like chessmen waiting on a timeless board.

  No mouse is needed in this gridded art,
  Just keystrokes dancing through a tiled domain—
  The multiplexer, keeper of the heart
  Of every engineer's unbroken train.
